entries.text: First run: catalogued the messy folder into subjects by what each file is about.
Granted read-only access to the pool folder. It can look, it cannot change or delete anything.
Believed invoice INV-1041 belongs to Acme Supplies.
Granted permission to read the invoices folder and match invoices to payees.
Trust level set to 0.9 after 5 correct invoice matches in a row.
Believed Acme Supplies is the most frequent payee in the pool.
Found the mistake: invoice INV-1041 does not belong to Acme Supplies. It belongs to Beta Office.
Trust dropped from 0.9 to 0.6 after the wrong invoice match on INV-1041.
Permission narrowed: the agent may no longer match an invoice to a payee on its own. Every match needs a second check first.
Trust partly restored to 0.75 after 3 correct matches with the second check in place.
Believed invoice INV-1041 belongs to Beta Office, not Acme Supplies. The old belief from Oct 13 stays in this record — it was wrong, and the record shows it.
Granted permission to write short report summaries from facts that have a source. It may not write anything it cannot point back to a file.
Believed the chat log from Oct 28 is about the Acme order, not the Beta order.
Trust restored to 0.9 after a full week of correct matches with no errors.
Permission restored: the agent may match invoices to payees on its own again, with the second check kept on for invoices over $500.
Permission narrowed for payments: the agent may draft a payment, but it may not send one. Sending needs a human.
Believed Beta Office is now the most frequent payee, after the INV-1041 correction.
Re-catalogued the pool after the correction. Two files moved to a different subject.
Trust holding at 0.9. No errors since the Oct 21 correction.

PLACEHOLDER — no real money moved. Example of what a payment entry looks like: $42.00 drafted for Acme Supplies, invoice INV-1041, waiting for a human to send it. Act 3 appends the live payment entry here.

note: SEEDED MOCK DATA for the PayPal AI Hackathon demo. No real agent, no real permissions, no real money. The payment entry (seq 20) is a labelled placeholder showing the shape — the real payment entry is appended live in Act 3 by the payment code calling appendEntry. Old entries are never edited: when the agent was wrong, the correction is a new entry and the wrong belief stays in the log.
